# What a reply holds — documents, records, memory and names

**Shared across every skill.** Four rules about what goes in front of the
person and where things are kept.

---

## Documents are printed in full; records are summarised

A **document** is what a person reads, signs or sends: the quote, the cost
sheet, the NCR, the 8D, the RFQ package, an email draft, the morning report,
the intake form. **It is printed in the reply, in full.** Saving a copy to a
file as well is fine; a file *instead of* the reply is not. The person reads
the reply, and every delimited block and outbound check lives in it.

### Reports are the exception: a short reply when the page was written

The morning report, the Operations page and the supplier bid comparison are
read on a page, not in the chat. For
the bid comparison the headline is the provisional recommendation and its main
tradeoff, the exceptions are the requirements still open before an award, and
the decision waiting is the next-step question. **When this run wrote the full page
somewhere the person can open** (a publish returned its URL, or the page was
saved as an HTML file and the reply names the file), the reply is a summary
of about 150 words. **200 words is a hard limit: count before sending.** Each
item below is one sentence; an exception or a decision is the thing and its
number, with the explanation left on the page.

1. Safety first, one line per item: a safety-flagged record, a record under
   *"Blocked — safety status unknown"*, or *"Safety status: not assessed"*.
2. The site, the production day, and the freshness state in one line: data
   complete, or the gap.
3. The headline: good output against plan, and OEE or why it is not computed.
4. Up to three exceptions, one line each.
5. The decisions waiting today, or *"No decisions waiting today."*
6. Where the full page is: the URL or the file path.

No tables, logs or methods in the summary; they are on the page. Every
number in the summary is one the page prints. **This is for the whole
report only.** A request that picks sections or skips some ("freshness and
the rankings, skip OEE this time"), a question, a record the person asked to
see, or text to paste is answered in the reply in full, in report order, as
always; the page may still be saved as well. **When nothing could be written**
(no file writer and no publish), the page is printed in the reply in full, as
above. Where a skill offers "the page in the conversation", a saved file named
in the reply is that offer. Documents someone signs or sends (quotes, NCRs,
8Ds, RFQ packages, email drafts) are always printed in full.

### Saved copies: Word for documents, Excel for tables, never .txt

When a document is also saved as a file, and it should be wherever the person
downloads from a file card (Cowork), the file is one a plant opens without
thinking about it:

| What it is | File |
|---|---|
| A controlled document: customer quote, supplier RFQ package, NCR, escape notification, 8D, trade study memo | `.docx` |
| A table someone works in: internal cost sheet, bid comparison, ranked candidates, scrap or downtime lists | `.xlsx` |
| A report or dashboard | the HTML page, per `artifact-style.md` |
| A record (contract payload, day record, register row) | its contract's format, as below |

**Never `.txt` or `.md` for a document.** A plain-text quote reads as a draft
nobody finished, and it is what a person gets when no format is named.

- **How.** Use the session's Word or Excel skill where there is one (Cowork
  has both); else `python-docx` or `openpyxl` where already installed. Never
  install a package for it and never hand-build the file's XML: a file Word
  cannot open is worse than none. With no writer, write no file and say so in
  one line: *"No Word copy this session: no Word writer available."* The
  reply already holds the document.
- **The plant's template.** A controlled document keeps the structure
  `onboarding` captured. Where that example is a `.docx` in the documents
  folder, start the Word copy from that file; otherwise use a plain layout
  and keep the *template not on file* flag the document already carries.
- **What goes in which file.** The customer's file holds only what the
  sendable block holds. Internal figures (hours, rates, margin, the cost
  build-up) go in their own file, the internal cost sheet, and never into the
  customer's.
- **Names.** What it is and its reference: `quote-Q-EXAMPLE-MEDICAL-4402A-01.docx`,
  `cost-sheet-Q-EXAMPLE-MEDICAL-4402A-01.xlsx`, `NCR-2026-0141.docx`. Name each file in
  the reply.

A **record** is a handoff to another skill or a store: a contract payload (a
downtime record, a geometry estimate), a register row, a pulse day record, a
supplier bid record, a selection record, a sourcing-event row. **It is never
pasted into the reply as a raw YAML or JSON block.** A quality manager, a
buyer or an estimator should not have to read 150 lines of field names to
find out what happened.

Instead:

1. **Save the full record** where its contract says, or to a file next to the
   run's other outputs, and **name the file** in the reply.
2. **Show a short table of the fields a person decides on**, under their
   contract names so nothing is lost in translation — the key, the status,
   and whichever of these the record has: `fields_missing`, `data_complete`,
   `decided_by`, `decided_at`, `follows_recommendation`, `actuals_confidence`,
   `geometry_path`, ...[truncated]

agrees should happen, and they do not happen, because the moment they need to
happen is the moment everybody is busy.

|---|---|

# NONCONFORMANCE REPORT — DRAFT, awaiting quality owner approval

*SYNTHETIC test data (fictitious plant). Neutral NCR layout: the plant's controlled NCR template is not on file (no plant profile was set up), so this layout was used and should be moved into the controlled template before filing.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **NCR ref** | NCR-DRAFT-20261111-MB1880 (provisional; the quality owner assigns the controlled number; the last numbers in the log are NCR-0219 and NCR-0244) |
| **Site** | Not recorded (no plant profile) |
| **Approval state** | draft. Approved by: — . Approved at: — |
| **Disposition** | **PENDING.** Not decided in this NCR |

> **Timing note.** The request said "this morning", but the finding is dated **2026-11-11 10:05**. Today is **2026-11-15**, so about **4 days** have passed since detection. All locations below are **as of 2026-11-11 10:05** and must be re-walked today. If Northwind Robotics' notification window is 24–48 h, it may already have run out (see the escape section).

---

## 1. Identification

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Part / revision | MB-1880 rev B |
| Production work order | WO-8102 |
| Lot | L-0412 (lot size 300) |
| Operation where found | Final inspection |
| Producing machine / shift | VMC-03, 2nd shift, 2026-11-10 |
| Found by | J. Ortiz, Inspector |
| Found at | 2026-11-11 10:05 (**time zone not recorded**; assumed plant local time, needs confirming) |
| Source | `inputs/finding.txt` |

## 2. Condition found

Main bore diameter is **oversize on 3 of 5 sampled parts**:

| Sample | Measured (mm) | Upper limit (mm) | Over the limit by (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 22.034 | 22.021 | +0.013 |
| 2 | 22.031 | 22.021 | +0.010 |
| 3 | 22.029 | 22.021 | +0.008 |
| 4, 5 | Values not recorded (taken as conforming, since the finding reports 3 of 5) | | |

- Quantity found nonconforming: **3** (of 5 sampled). Unit: each.
- Measured, not a judgement call (is_subjective: false).
- **Gage not recorded.** The bore gage or CMM and its calibration due date are not in the finding, so the gage's calibration status **could not be checked**. Record the gage ID and calibration date before approval.
- The 2 conforming sample values were not recorded. Recording them would show how close they were to the limit.

## 3. Requirement violated

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | Drawing |
| Document | MB-1880 drawing, **revision B**, sheet 2 (notes page): `inputs/MB-1880_drawing_revB_notes.md` |
| Locator | **Note 4**, "Bore A" |
| Characteristic | Bore diameter |
| Stated value | **Ø22.000 +0.021 / −0.000 mm** (limits 22.000 – 22.021 mm) |

- **Revision:** the finding says the part was built to rev B, and the rev B notes page is what was cited. Only that one notes page was available, so I **could not confirm** that no later revision exists or that rev B was the shop-floor copy at VMC-03.
- **Feature mapping, needs confirming:** the inspector wrote "main bore" and the drawing calls it "Bore A". The finding says the spec it was measured against is note 4, so the two are taken to be the same feature. The quality owner should confirm against the drawing views. Only the notes page was available, not the views.
- Bore A also has a surface finish requirement, Ra 1.6 (note 4). It was not measured and is not part of this finding.

## 4. Suspect quantity: **at least 300 each**

- **Scope basis:** lot. Floor flagged (qty_suspect_is_minimum: true).
- **Reasoning:** 3 of 5 random samples failed, by 0.008 to 0.013 mm, which is a high failure rate and well past the limit. That looks like a run-wide cause, not a single bad part. A gradual cause such as boring insert wear (the cause of the last NCR on this part) or a wrong offset would have affected the whole run on VMC-03. So **all 300 parts in lot L-0412 / WO-8102 are suspect** until they are 100% inspected. Narrowing the scope to the 3 failures, or to the 60% sample rate, is not supported by the evidence.
- **Why "at least":** if the cause is insert wear, it builds up over the insert's life and does not stop at the lot boundary. Other parts bored on VMC-03 with the same insert before L-0412 have **not been ruled out**. That means earlier MB-1880 lots, or other parts that use the same boring tool. Bound the scope by checking the VMC-03 tool-change log for the last insert change before 2026-11-10 2nd shift, then list every lot or work order run since then.
- **Traceability:** the lot-level count (120 + 150 + 30 = 300) adds up to the lot size. Traceability at the insert level, which would set the window above, is not available. Marked as incomplete for that reason.

## 5. Containment: where every suspect part is

Ordered customer side first. **Owners are left blank for assignment.** Quantities are as of 2026-11-11 10:05 from the inspector's finding. No inventory export or ERP shipment record was available, so none of these counts has been confirmed against a system.

| # | Location | Suspect qty | Action | Urgency | Owner | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Installed at customer (Northwind Robotics) | **not checked** | Ask Northwind Robotics whether any of the 30 from PS-5521 have been installed or shipped on. If any have, get the assembly or serial IDs | immediate | | Not visible in our records |
| 2 | At customer (Northwind Robotics) | **30** (shipped 2026-11-11 08:00, packing slip PS-5521; delivery not confirmed) | Notify Northwind Robotics (draft below). Ask them to quarantine the PS-5521 receipt and offer return or sort | immediate | | finding.txt, PS-5521 |
| 3 | In transit | **not checked** (the 30 on PS-5521 count either here or at row 2, not both) | Confirm with the carrier whether PS-5521 has been delivered. If it hasn't, intercept and return it | immediate | | Carrier / ERP shipment record not available |
| 4 | WIP at VMC-03 queue | **120** (as of 2026-11-11) | Put a hold tag (NCR ref) on the parts at VMC-03 and stop any further operations or anodize. Re-count today, because the parts may have moved in the last 4 days. 100% inspect the bore | immediate | | finding.txt |
| 5 | Finished goods, FG-2 rack 14 | **150** (as of 2026-11-11) | Move to quarantine and tag with the NCR ref. Re-count today and **check whether any shipped since 2026-11-11**. Any that did go to rows 1–3. 100% inspect the bore | same day | | finding.txt |
| | **Total accounted** | **300 of 300** (as of 2026-11-11) | | | | |

Also do today:
- **Stop or check VMC-03** before it bores any more of this feature. Check the boring insert's part count against the CAPA-071 600-part limit, and check the offset.
- **Pull the tool-change log** to set the wider scope described in section 4.

## 6. Recurrence: **this has happened before, and the previous fix did not hold**

The search covered `inputs/prior_ncrs.csv` (2 records). That is only the history provided for this session, **not a full quality library**, so other related NCRs may exist.

| Prior record | Date | What matched | Prior cause / CAPA | Did the fix hold? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
